title: NonAtomicResumeOnConsumedNextIndex
description: Resume after a partially-broadcast run can re-register a fresh NudgeRatchet at the wrong index. registerDispatcher consumes NFTMinterV2.nextIndex (7 -> 8). Under `--skip-simulation --slow`, the progress file is flushed via `vm.writeFile` AFTER the registration tx lands. A crash in the tx-land-to-flush gap leaves the on-chain index consumed (now 8) while the progress file still says the step is pending. On re-run, the script redeploys and re-registers, landing at index 8, and the inline `require(ratchetIndex == 7)` drift guard reverts, halting the resume. The originally-registered ratchet is left orphaned/stranded at index 7.
impact: Operational availability hazard on resume only. No asset loss and no theft path: the condition is recoverable via manual progress-file repair, requires a crash inside a narrow non-atomic window, and is owner-operated. The originally-registered ratchet at index 7 is stranded but not lost. A competent non-malicious operator would be surprised that a mid-broadcast crash bricks the resume rather than continuing it (Law-3 footgun test passes).
evidence: registerDispatcher consumes NFTMinterV2.nextIndex 7 -> 8 as a side effect of registration.
Progress is persisted with vm.writeFile only AFTER the registration tx under `--skip-simulation --slow`, creating a tx-land-to-flush gap.
A crash in that gap yields on-chain nextIndex already advanced (8) but progress file marking the step incomplete.
Re-run path redeploys + re-registers, the new registration lands at index 8, and inline `require(ratchetIndex == 7)` reverts and halts the resume.
Orphaned ratchet remains registered at index 7 with no automatic reclamation.
attackPath: registerDispatcher tx lands on-chain, advancing NFTMinterV2.nextIndex 7 -> 8.
Process crashes before vm.writeFile flushes progress.
Operator re-runs to resume; script redeploys and re-registers a fresh NudgeRatchet, which lands at index 8.
Inline require(ratchetIndex == 7) reverts; resume halts; the index-7 ratchet is orphaned.
recommendation: Make the progress flush atomic with (or strictly before) the consuming tx, or add an idempotent already-registered pre-check before redeploy/re-register so resume detects the consumed index and continues rather than redeploying. The `require(ratchetIndex == 7)` assertion is a correct drift guard and must be retained; it is the redeploy-on-resume that should be made idempotent.
